newsitem.title: USA: Poll says Americans favor historic heroes.
newsitem.headline: Poll says Americans favor historic heroes.

text.p: Heroes are an endangered species in the United States, according to a poll conducted by the Yankelovich company for "Life" magazine and released on Thursday.
The poll, which will appear in a special edition of the magazine to hit newsstands on Monday, said 63 percent of Americans feel there are fewer heroic figures today than in the past.

The poll said the most revered living heroes are Mother Theresa (81 percent of respondents), former military leader Colin Powell (65 percent), basketball star Michael Jordan (40 percent), and President Clinton (26 percent).
In addition, 70 percent of respondents said their fathers were heroes and 80 percent named their mothers.
The two most heroic figures cited were Abraham Lincoln (89 percent) and Martin Luther King, Jr. (82 percent).
